analysis.title: DeskTalk - The US consumer splits in two
key_insights: Recent CPI report and Fedspeak strengthened the case for further tightening and higher-for-longer rates, but credit card data shows a more K-shaped US consumer beneath headline resilience.
NY Fed: credit card balances hit a record $1.29tn in Q3 2026, +1.7% from Q2. Total household debt (mortgages, student and auto loans included) rose $334 billion.
Delinquency rates are falling, but the gap between borrowers in higher-income and lower-income neighborhoods has widened.

U Mich sentiment beat expectations last month, but the underlying data is increasingly K-shaped. After the recent AI-led equity selloff, confidence rose among lower- and middle-wealth consumers and fell 5% for those with the largest stock portfolios. The high-income vs low-income gap persists.

For the Fed, cooling demand could raise the bar for further tightening. A deeper equity selloff would weaken higher-income consumption, and wider credit spreads would add pressure on lower-income borrowers. This could limit the chance of the 75bp of hikes currently priced by OIS markets, though the impact may take time to emerge.
Holiday season should give the sector some relief. Mastercard forecasts sales +5.5% YoY in 2026, and earnings should show solid outlooks.
Citi Research says persistent inflation and higher gas prices are overshadowed by a solid jobs backdrop and a positive wealth effect from higher asset prices.

Consumer earnings are the next test: Home Depot (Nov 17), TJX and Target (Nov 18), Walmart (Nov 19), Costco (Dec 10). Walmart and Costco remain consensus longs but have recently been used as funding shorts by many hedge funds.
Citi's Airlines team finds that supermajors are well positioned to capitalize on K-shaped trends.

tension_points.bull_case: Holiday spending (Mastercard forecasts +5.5% YoY) and solid earnings outlooks, supported by a solid jobs backdrop and positive wealth effect from higher asset prices, per Citi Research.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit card balances are at a record $1.29tn and the gap between lower- and higher-income borrowers is widening. Wealthy consumers' sentiment fell 5% after the equity selloff, and a deeper selloff or wider credit spreads would hit both groups.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deeper equity selloff or wider credit spreads, or weak holiday spending and consumer earnings next week (Home Depot Nov 17, TJX and Target Nov 18, Walmart Nov 19).
